scenes.heading: Avoiding burnout when writing is both craft and business

sents.d: Avoiding burnout when writing is both craft and business
Treating writing purely as inspiration-driven work makes it hard to run as a business.

Writing is often taught as an inspiration-driven creative act, but running it as a business requires treating it partly as a repeatable process — deadlines, invoicing, client management — which can feel at odds with the craft side if not managed deliberately.

Batching similar tasks (all client emails at one time, all first drafts in a focused block, all editing in another) tends to protect deeper creative focus better than constantly switching between writing and administrative tasks throughout the day.

Building in buffer time between projects, rather than scheduling back-to-back deadlines with no breathing room, reduces the likelihood of the kind of burnout that leads to declining quality or resenting otherwise good client relationships.

take: Batch your work and protect buffer time to avoid burnout.
